item.title: How China and Russia Can Exploit the Iran War
item.description: In Foreign Affairs, Jon B. Alterman and Ali Vaez argue China and Russia can exploit an Iran war by letting the U.S. bear the costs. They gain influence and advance strategic aims while avoiding direct conflict.

item.title: Mona Yacoubian in Foreign Policy: Lebanon’s Moment of Reckoning
item.description: The Lebanese government faces a moment of reckoning, with Israel, with Hezbollah, and with the Lebanese people.

item.title: NATO’S Hidden Dividend and the Avoidable Cost of U.S. Withdrawal
item.description: NATO was designed to do more than provide security, it built deep economic integration that has become one of its least appreciated strengths. The economic gains are large, durable, and, in many cases, effectively self-financing relative to the costs of membership.

item.title: Governing Antarctica in 2026
item.description: CSIS Americas Program Senior Associate Bill Muntean gives an overview of the agenda and issues for the upcoming Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting.

item.title: Toward a Mature AI Economy: Policy Priorities for the Road Ahead
item.description: To encourage long-term innovative uses of AI that go beyond simple process improvements, policymakers should focus beyond the tech industry, provide clarity on data privacy, and support foundational training on AI.

item.title: Why Open-Source Intelligence Is a Powerful Weapon Against Fentanyl
item.description: The fentanyl crisis is one of the most urgent public health and national security concerns facing the United States. Combatting it will require the know-how and access of industry partners working with the authorities and resources of the U.S. government and its allies.

item.title: The Rule of Holes
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch describes the effect the war in Iran is having on energy prices, transitions to green energy, and vulnerabilities of Gulf states.

item.title: The Strait of Hormuz in 8 Charts
item.description: As the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz drags on, new vessel-tracking and trade data reveal the state of play in the strait and explore how the crisis is rattling global markets.

item.title: States Weekly: April 22, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers April 22, 2026.

item.title: North Korea as It Is: The Case for a Cold Peace
item.description: After three decades and seven presidential administrations of the same denuclearization framework, North Korea's arsenal has only grown. CSIS's Victor Cha argues in Foreign Affairs that it's time to stop pretending the old framework can work and instead build a "cold peace."
